messages:
alex: FYI: CI artifact signing is moving off runner-local keys onto the new centralized signer (workflow-signer) on 2026-04-20. Maintenance window: 2026-04-20 00:00 -> 2026-04-21 12:00 UTC.

meera: TL;DR: stop using private keys on self-hosted runners. Replace with the GH action or the service API that accepts OIDC tokens. This is mandatory for any repo that publishes signed artifacts.

dylan: Any quick migration example?

meera: Example GH action step: 
```
- id: oidc
  uses: redwood/get-oidc-token@v1
- uses: redwood/workflow-signer@v1
  with:
    oidc-token: ${{ steps.oidc.outputs.token }}
    artifact-path: ./build/output.tgz
```
Also add IAM binding: role "signer.invoke" to service account signer-sa@redwood-internal.

alex: Canary plan: infra/* -> internal-tools/* -> public-services/*. First canary build 02:00 UTC on the 20th for one infra repo, monitor 120m.

secops-bot: POLICY: Runner-local signing keys must be rotated and disabled by 2026-04-19. Exceptions require an approved SecOps ticket.

dylan: What if a pipeline calls the old "sign-artifact" binary directly?

meera: Those need a small shim to call the signer API. We will publish a compatibility binary that proxies to the signer for 7 days after cutover. Do not rely on that long-term.

infra-oncall: Rollback knobs: 1) re-enable runner signing (emergency only), 2) toggle org-wide feature flag to allow legacy action input `legacy: true` (available 24h after cutover). Use infra-oncall for any urgent rollback.

alex: Action items: 1) update workflows this week, 2) run canary and confirm attestation logs, 3) file exceptions if you cant migrate. Ill drop the checklist + PR template in #devex in 1hr.

meera: If you hit "auth token missing" errors, check that your workflow requested an OIDC token and that the signer service IAM binding exists.

dylan: Ill scan our repos for runner-local signing usage and ping owners.

alex: Thanks everyone. Well post status updates in this thread during the migration window. :thumbsup:
